title: The Two Adams
hookLine: Rabbi Joseph Soloveitchik described two sides of every person: the builder and the lonely seeker
carry: both adams, builder and seeker, are willed by god
tomorrow: why would a rabbi care exactly when the sun sets?

cards: Noa's palms still smell like sawdust. She built most of the set for the spring show this week: measured, cut, hammered, painted. Everyone loved it.
Then at the cast party she stood by the snacks and felt invisible. Can the same person build skyscrapers and still feel alone? Rabbi Joseph Soloveitchik said yes, and that both are holy.
He found the answer by noticing that the Torah tells the making of the first human twice.

teach.b: In his essay The Lonely Man of Faith, Soloveitchik reads the two creation stories as two sides of every person. In the first chapter, the human is made in God's image and told to "replenish the earth, and subdue it."
He calls this Adam the first: the builder. Curious, bold, asking how the world works, making tools, cities, medicines. That's a calling, not a lapse.
In the second chapter, the human is formed from the dust and set in a garden "to dress it and to keep it." And then God says, "It is not good that the man should be alone."
That's Adam the second: the seeker. He asks why, and who am I, and longs to be known, by God and by another person. Here's the line worth sharing tonight.
Soloveitchik didn't treat the two chapters as a contradiction to fix. He treated them as a portrait of us.
Both Adams are willed by God, and a person moves between them all life long.

teach.h: BOTH ADAMS, BUILDER AND SEEKER, ARE WILLED BY GOD.
teach.b: The builder can't cure the seeker's loneliness with a bigger project. And the seeker's loneliness isn't a failure. In his telling, it's part of what faith feels like from the inside.

how: The Lonely Man of Faith is read in Jewish study groups and classes on modern Jewish thought, often beside the first two chapters of Genesis.

o: a craftsman who builds a house of prayer
a pilgrim who travels to find a holy place
two sides in everyone: one masters, one longs

p: the builder: replenish the earth, subdue it
the seeker: longs to be known
to dress it and to keep it
not good that the man should be alone

s: Soloveitchik treats the two creation stories as a contradiction to fix
he reads them as two sides of every person.
for Soloveitchik, both the builder and the seeker are willed by God
building is a calling too, not a lapse.
for Soloveitchik, the seeker's loneliness means faith has failed
he describes it as part of what faith feels like from inside.

games.q: your dad runs his company brilliantly, but at night he says he doesn't know what it's all for. what would Soloveitchik's two Adams say?
o: both are him: the builder is doing well, and the seeker's question is real too.
the question means he should quit and find something meaningful.
a bigger success will settle the question once and for all.
games.why: Soloveitchik says both Adams are willed by God. the builder's success doesn't cure the seeker's longing, and isn't meant to.

practice: Rest your hands on your knees. Close your right hand into a loose fist: the builder, everything you made or fixed this week. Turn your left hand open, palm up: the seeker, what you're still hoping for.
Stay with both hands, and let neither one win.

wordCard.voice: Builder and seeker: Soloveitchik's two Adams, the one who masters the world and the one who longs to be known, both living in each of us.

orig.note: Hebrew: human being; Adam. Soloveitchik's Adam the first and Adam the second.

carryVoice: The line to keep: both Adams, builder and seeker, are willed by God. A full calendar and a lonely heart can belong to the same good person.
